metadata.name: Malaysia Medical Bill Reference Price Table
metadata.purpose: Reference dataset for flagging potential overcharges/errors on Malaysian medical bills (Sabah Smart City hackathon MVP). Oriented toward checking PRIVATE hospital/clinic bills, with government (MOH) rates included as context/floor.
IMPORTANT_READ_FIRST: Only DOCTORS' professional fees are legally capped in Malaysia (PHFSA 1998 / Regulations 2006: Schedule 7 for GP clinics, Schedule 13 for specialists in private hospitals). These are MAXIMUM chargeable fees.

Ward charges, facility fees, lab tests, imaging and DRUGS in the private sector are NOT price-regulated. For these, the table gives an advisory benchmark only. Your tool must flag them as 'above typical range - worth querying', NOT as 'illegal' or 'fraud'.

Every item has a 'verified' flag. verified=true means the number is backed by a cited government/legal source. verified=false means it is INDICATIVE only and MUST be replaced with a real lookup (e.g. MyPriMe for drugs) before any live demo.
Government (MOH) rates apply to Malaysian citizens and are heavily subsidised. Non-citizens pay much higher amended-2017 rates (see non_citizen_note).

reference_type_legend.legal_cap: A legally gazetted maximum chargeable fee. Charging above this is a genuine violation.
reference_type_legend.advisory_benchmark: A published but non-binding reference (e.g. MyPriMe). Use for 'above typical' flags only.
reference_type_legend.market_range: Typical observed market range from surveys/reporting. Not official. Use for context and soft flags only.
reference_type_legend.government_rate: Subsidised MOH rate for citizens. Used as a floor/context, never as the expected private price.

flag_rule_hint.explanation: Suggested starting rule: flag if billed_price > reference_max * 1.2. Tune per item. For legal_cap items, flag ANY amount above reference_max, not just 1.2x.

primary_sources: Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998 (Act 586) and Regulations 2006 - Schedule 7 (GP) & Schedule 13 (specialist) professional fees
Private Healthcare Facilities and Services (Amendment) Order 2013 - increased professional fees by 14.4%

MMA MPSN® - Medical Procedures and Services Nomenclature and Relative Values Guidelines, Malaysian Medical Association, 5th Edition Version 2.0 (2020) — Malaysia's standard procedure coding guide used by hospitals, insurers and managed care organisations nationwide
Malaysia Medicine Price Guide / MyPriMe (formerly Consumer Price Guide), Pharmaceutical Services Programme MOH - https://pharmacy.moh.gov.my/en/apps/drug-price
MOH Malaysia, CodeBlue (Galen Centre), Malay Mail reporting on gazetted fee orders

mpsn_explanation.what_it_is: Malaysia's standard procedure nomenclature and relative values guide — the local equivalent of US CPT codes. Provides standardised procedure codes and a relative value scale for billing. Used by hospitals, insurance companies, managed care organisations, and third-party administrators across Malaysia.
mpsn_explanation.relationship_to_schedule_13: Schedule 13 of PHFSA sets the MAXIMUM fee caps. MPSN provides the PROCEDURE CODES and RELATIVE VALUES to identify what was actually billed. Together they are used to detect upcoding (billing a higher-code procedure than what was done) and miscoding — the same logic US apps use with CPT codes.
mpsn_explanation.how_to_use_in_system: When a bill lists a procedure name, match it to its MPSN code. Then check the billed fee against the Schedule 13 cap for that procedure code. This two-step check (code match + price check) is the most rigorous approach.
mpsn_explanation.proposed_partner_role: Frame in pitch as: 'procedure matching powered by MMA MPSN codes, price benchmarked against PHFSA Schedule 13 caps, with MMA as the validating body for the reference data'.

metadata.non_citizen_note: Under the Fees (Medical)(Amendment) Order 2017, non-citizens at MOH facilities pay much higher rates (e.g. outpatient ~RM40, specialist clinic ~RM120, third-class ward ~RM126/day). This table's government_rate figures are the citizen rates.
metadata.sst_note: From 1 July 2025 a 6% Sales & Service Tax applies to private healthcare facilities with taxable revenue above RM1.5 million. Doctors' consultation fees are service-tax EXEMPT. A bill may legitimately show 6% SST on non-exempt items.

items.name: GP consultation - first visit (private clinic)
items.source: PHFSA Schedule 7 (as amended 2013); DG of Health press statement 6 Mar 2014
items.mpsn_code: See MMA MPSN 5th Ed v2.0 (2020) — consultation codes Section A
items.flag_basis: Charging above RM125 exceeds the legal maximum professional fee for a GP consultation (Schedule 7). Any amount above this cap is a genuine regulatory violation.
items.notes: Government clinic outpatient consultation for citizens is ~RM1.

items.name: Specialist consultation - first visit (private hospital)
items.source: PHFSA Schedule 13 (as amended 2013); The Centre / 2013 Amendment Order
items.mpsn_code: See MMA MPSN 5th Ed v2.0 (2020) — specialist consultation codes Section A
items.flag_basis: Charging above RM235 exceeds the legal maximum professional fee for an initial specialist consultation (Schedule 13). Also flag if the MPSN procedure code does not match the billed specialty — a sign of upcoding.
items.notes: Government specialist clinic follow-up for citizens is ~RM5.

items.name: Specialist consultation - follow-up (private hospital)
items.source: Reported follow-up range under Schedule 13 (secondary source; confirm exact gazetted figure before demo)
items.mpsn_code: See MMA MPSN 5th Ed v2.0 (2020) — follow-up consultation codes
items.flag_basis: Follow-up fee must be lower than the first-visit cap. Also flag if a follow-up visit is miscoded as a first visit to charge the higher rate — a common upcoding pattern detectable via MPSN.
items.notes: VERIFY exact Schedule 13 figure before demo. MPSN distinguishes initial vs follow-up visits clearly.

items.name: Ward charge per day - general ward (private hospital)
items.source: Market survey figures (calculatormalaysia 2026, secondary). NOT regulated.
items.flag_basis: Ward/accommodation is not price-regulated; flag only if far above typical market range and cross-check the hospital's published rate card.
items.notes: Government third-class ward is ~RM3/day; first-class ~RM120/day (Fees Medical Order 2017). Private is set by each hospital.

items.name: Normal delivery (private hospital)
items.source: Market survey figures (secondary). Doctor's delivery fee component is capped under Schedule 13; facility component is not.
items.flag_basis: Split doctor professional fee (capped) from facility/ward charges (not capped) when reviewing.
items.notes: Government third-class normal delivery for citizens is ~RM10.

items.name: Outpatient registration / consultation (government)
items.flag_basis: Government outpatient is RM1 (RM5 for specialist follow-up) for citizens.

items.name: Angiogram / single-stent angioplasty
items.source: The Centre (secondary), citing MOH & PHFSA context
items.flag_basis: Wide range; use as ballpark only and separate the capped doctor fee from facility/consumables.
items.notes: Public hospital range for citizens is roughly RM50-200.

items.name: Coronary bypass surgery (CABG)
items.notes: Public hospital cost for citizens is roughly RM4,000.

items.name: Dengue treatment / admission
items.notes: Free at public hospitals for citizens.

items.name: Targeted therapy dose (government reference)
items.flag_basis: Government charges RM50 (third class) to RM600 (first class) per dose.
items.notes: Context reference for how class affects government pricing.

items.name: X-ray (basic)
items.source: INDICATIVE ONLY - replace with a real private hospital rate card before demo
items.notes: Government x-ray for citizens is very low (single-digit to ~RM10 range depending on class/type).

items.name: Full Blood Count (FBC)
items.source: INDICATIVE ONLY - replace with a real private lab/hospital rate card before demo
items.notes: Basic tests are covered/nominal at government facilities for citizens.

items.name: Paracetamol 500mg tablet
items.source: Malaysia Medicine Price Guide (MyPriMe), Pharmaceutical Services Programme MOH. Data updated August 2025. https://pharmacy.moh.gov.my/en/apps/drug-price
items.flag_basis: These are SUGGESTED retail prices from product registration holders — not hard price caps. Flag if billed significantly above RM0.70/tablet. Note: private clinics bundle dispensing margin; a reasonable clinic retail price may be up to RM1.00/tablet. Flag anything well above RM1.00.
items.notes: Most common drug prescribed in Malaysian primary care. Generic versions as low as RM0.16/tablet. Brand markup is real but not regulated.

items.name: Amoxicillin 500mg capsule
items.source: Malaysia Medicine Price Guide (MyPriMe), Pharmaceutical Services Programme MOH. Data updated August 2025. https://pharmacy.moh.gov.my/en/apps/drug-price
items.flag_basis: Suggested retail price range RM0.28–RM0.85/capsule. Flag if billed significantly above RM0.85/capsule. Typical 5-day course = 15 capsules; watch for unreasonably large quantities billed for a short illness.
items.notes: Second most commonly prescribed drug in Malaysian GP clinics. Price varies by brand; generic is very cheap.

items.name: Cetirizine 10mg tablet
items.source: Malaysia Medicine Price Guide (MyPriMe), Pharmaceutical Services Programme MOH. Data updated August 2025. https://pharmacy.moh.gov.my/en/apps/drug-price
items.flag_basis: Suggested retail price range RM0.22–RM0.63/tablet. Flag if billed significantly above RM0.70/tablet.
items.notes: Common antihistamine for allergies. Third most prescribed drug class in Malaysian GP clinics.

items.name: Diclofenac Sodium 50mg tablet
items.source: Malaysia Medicine Price Guide (MyPriMe), Pharmaceutical Services Programme MOH. Data updated August 2025. https://pharmacy.moh.gov.my/en/apps/drug-price
items.flag_basis: Suggested retail price RM0.28–RM0.32/tablet (very narrow range). Note: SR (slow-release) 75mg and 100mg variants are higher (RM0.41–RM0.44). Flag if billed significantly above RM0.50/tablet for the standard 50mg.
items.notes: Common NSAID painkiller/anti-inflammatory. Very affordable generic. Flag if billed at the same price as the branded SR variant.

items.name: Nursing care charge per day (private)
items.source: INDICATIVE ONLY - not regulated; replace with real rate card before demo
items.flag_basis: Not regulated; benchmark only. Watch for nursing billed separately AND bundled into ward charge (possible double-billing).
items.notes: A good candidate for a duplicate/unbundling check.
